text:
maya: quick follow-up from the RFC — proposing a staged deprecation path for the legacy project-scoped API key surface. want to align on rollout windows and migration UX.

alex: thanks. can you summarise the stages? short bullets are fine.

maya: sure — thinking 3 stages: 1) soft-warning header + telemetry (30d), 2) opt-in enforcement with partner toggle (60d), 3) mandatory enforcement + sunset docs (30d). totals ~120d.

sam: is the main risk that internal customers won't update? we have a few infra customers on pinned workflows.

maya: yes. also cross-org integrations that rely on unscoped api keys. we should support a migration shim: issue scoped tokens on behalf of legacy keys for a limited time.

alex: how would the shim work technically? oauth exchange flow or server-side mint?

maya: server-side mint. flow: legacy key -> auth-service verifies -> issue short-lived scoped token (1h) tied to project/org mapping. we log and rate-limit.

maya: config snippet for rollout policy (Pseudocode):
```
rollout:
  stage1: warning_header: true, telemetry: true
  stage2: enforcement: optional, config_flag: allow_legacy_mint
  stage3: enforcement: required, legacy_mint: off
  migration_shim_ttl: 90d
```

priya: important: any minting implies additional audit surface and potential for privilege escalation. we need strict mapping rules and a manual review for ambiguous keys.

maya: agreed. plan is to refuse mint for ambiguous mappings and notify owner. add an admin review queue.

sam: product asks: how will SDKs indicate deprecation to end-users? email/console banners?

alex: console banner + per-key warning in API keys page. also SDKs get a `deprecationWarning` field in responses during stage1.

maya: decision question for eng-security: do we allow legacy keys to map to org-wide scoped tokens, or must we always narrow to project scope? tradeoff: convenience vs least-privilege.

priya: security stance: prefer narrow (project) by default. allow org-wide only when explicit owner approval recorded.

sam: ops complexity increases if too strict. customers might break large pipelines. maybe a policy exception workflow?

maya: propose default narrow + exception flow (ticketed, timeboxed). add telemetry to measure impact.

alex: rollout timeline suggestion: start stage1 in 2 weeks, run 30d. stage2 opt-in at +30d for 60d. stage3 at +90d. can we shorten if telemetry shows low breakage?

maya: yes, shorten path if <1% of keys still using legacy behavior after stage2.

security-bot: notice: created issue RED-2384 to track migration shim implementation and admin queue.

alex: one more: runtime routing — when mint is on, route legacy-key requests through auth-mint cluster. ensure we don't overload serving path. add circuit-breaker and separate quotas.

maya: added to RED-2384. will draft a short RFC update with the exact API headers and admin UI mocks.

priya: thumbs up. also add an audit-only opt-in for customers who want to test enforcement before breakage.

sam: ok to proceed with timeline. i'll loop in support docs owner to draft migration guides.

maya: thanks all — i'll put the RFC follow-up with timeline and implementation checklist here by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
